counterfactual.change: reduced body vx from 45.067 to 10.0 only; slower face impact is resolved without penetration, proving failure depends on high approach speed vs thin wall

explanation: High-speed (~45 m/s) head-on hit on left face of thin wall (h=0.28, x=7.038). Contact is detected (distance goes +0.098 at step16 to -0.040 at step17 to -0.178 at step18) but velocity vx stays exactly 45.067 across steps 15-18, so neither impulse nor positional correction acts. Penetration then grows by the full per-step displacement (~0.138) and exceeds the 0.15 limit at step 18. Likely cause: box-circle solver fails to resolve face contacts when wall thickness is much smaller than diameter combined with large per-step momentum, or substepped correction is capped too small.
vision_note: The red circle moves rightward toward the left end of the thin horizontal wall. It fails to bounce or stop and instead progressively embeds into the wall through steps 16 to 18.
